title: Carl Friedrich Gauss's birth chart
metaDescription: Carl Friedrich Gauss's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 10.4° Taurus. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Mars and Pluto sit 0.5° from an exact trine — near enough that the tradition reads drive and depth as a single working part. Trines are read as inheritance rather than achievement: the ease is genuine, and nothing about it was earned.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's exact place is 10.4° Taurus. That falls in the second decan, 10°–20°, sub-ruled by Mercury in the classical scheme — a earth sign read through a fixed season.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: The personal planets sit Mercury at 14.3° Taurus, Venus at 17.4° Gemini, Mars at 0.7° Libra. Mercury in a earth sign reads as a mind that trusts the measured and the checked; Venus in a air sign reads as taste led by wit and proportion; Mars in a air sign reads as drive that argues its way forward.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Mars to Pluto is the closest call of the day, a trine within 0.5°. A trine runs downhill — the talent that never announces itself because it never had to. Behind it, Saturn square Pluto at 0.9°, and the Sun conjunction Mercury at 3.9° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, three sit in a sign it has an opinion about. Mars in Libra at 0.7° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Jupiter in Cancer at 18.9° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Saturn in Libra at 29.3° is in exaltation. None of these labels is a verdict on a person; they describe how a function is situated, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Of the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: 6 in air, 3 in earth, 1 in water by element, 4 fixed, 3 mutable, 3 cardinal by modality. Air signs carry exchange in the scheme — comparison, argument, the sentence that makes the situation legible. No settled placement falls in fire — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Mars, Saturn and Neptune were retrograde. Pluto changed direction during the day, so its motion is left open.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Aquarius for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.2° between midnight and midnight. The missing clock moves the Moon by half a sign at most here, and the boundary was never close. At the noon reference it stands at 7.2°.
